abstract: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Notes (March 27, 2026) by Jessica Liu and Douglas Webber analyzing AI adoption and firms' job-posting behavior. Using Lightcast job postings and Census BTOS data (1.2M firms, Sept 2023 - Nov 2025), the authors find 'no evidence thus far that industries with higher levels of AI adoption are posting fewer jobs' and 'precisely-estimated null effects' at the firm level.
keyFindings: 'No evidence thus far that industries with higher levels of AI adoption are posting fewer jobs'
Firm-level analysis: 'precisely-estimated null effects' on job postings
45.9% of workers reported LLM use at work in June/July 2025 (up from 30.1% in Dec 2024)
Only 5.5% of firms had AI-related job postings in 2025
Analysis 'explicitly backward-looking' — does not forecast future labor impacts
methodology: Combines Lightcast job-postings database with Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS). Data period Sept 2023 - Nov 2025. Industry-level and firm-level regression analysis.
qualifiers: Authors emphasize backward-looking scope. Job postings are a leading indicator of hiring intent, not a direct measure of headcount changes. Compatible with the possibility that AI-driven displacement shows up in future data.
